title: Not really a game
content:
This app is disguised as a game, but it’s really an app designed to deliver a selection of ads over and over and over again. I’m at Level 629 at the moment and the ads now take up almost as much time as the game. Worse, many of the ads require to tap through 4 or more screens, some of which are design to take you to the App Store on the first tap, regardless where you tap. The close X in most ads is minute and so easy to miss. You quickly learn the sequences to get rid of the ads as they repeat and repeat and repeat. 

Yes I can pay the people to stop the ads, but I don’t believe that will do it. There will be more layers of different ads, because the game is incidental to the purpose of the app, which is to make money from ad views.

If you love ads, this is the app for you. But if you want to actually play a game, try something else, if you can find a genuinely ad-free application that includes a game.

title: Fun Game, Misleading Scam Ads
content:
I was really enjoying this game at first and would have happily given it a positive review. The levels are fun, relaxing, and a good way to pass time, but the advertising has completely ruined the experience. In the beginning, ads were mostly optional and could be watched for extra coins, which felt fair.
However, after reaching around level 50, the experience changed significantly. Forced ads started appearing after nearly every level, often long and intrusive, with no option to skip. It feels like the game becomes less about enjoyment and more about pushing ads once players are invested.
One of the ads shown in the game was a misleading fake warning claiming my device had been hacked / infected and that my account had been restricted. Ads like this are deceptive, alarming, and should not be allowed in a game downloaded from the App Store. It creates unnecessary panic and makes the app feel untrustworthy and it’s difficult to avoid because the game requires wifi to play.

It’s disappointing because the actual game is enjoyable, but allowing scam-style ads and forcing an undisclosed internet connection makes the overall experience frustrating also If the developers reduced the forced ads and made them more balanced like they were in the earlier levels, this would be a much better experience. I hope the developers review the ads they allow and become more transparent with players.

title: Fun overall but with some annoyances
content:
This is a compelling game that did a very good job of evoking that “just one more level” feeling. It starts easy but does ramp up in difficulty considerably; after a few hundred levels even the normal levels are tougher than the earlier “super hard” levels, and “super hard” levels now are pretty much impossible to win first try, for better or for worse.

Some of the mechanics are not my favourite. Canyon Chase is clearly fake multiplayer and vanishingly unlikely to be completable. Pilot’s Drop adds an unnecessary RNG element. Gates can screw you over by accidentally clearing a block when moving it out of the way. Being jumpscared by bomb blocks in a crate was cute once but just frustrating afterwards, and clearly meant to force the use of a time freeze given the extremely tight time limits.

My favourite mechanic is probably the ice gates, or the grey unclearable blocks.

title: I wanted a relaxing game. This isn’t one! And once you’re stuck, there’s no option but to spend cash
content:
This is a great game. The graphics work smoothly and the puzzles are engaging. I really enjoy it except for a couple of things. Unfortunately, they’re big things. Firstly, I was looking for a relaxing puzzle game. This isn’t one. The timers are extremely short so every level is a frantic rush of pushing blocks around. There’s little thought, planning or strategy, just rush rush rush. It actually puts my heart rate and stress level up. I’d like the option to play levels without the constant time pressure. It doesn’t add anything to the game for the players, but it does “encourage” us to use boosters, which make the devs more money.

The levels get very difficult very quickly and once you’re stuck on a level, it’s no longer possible to play. You have to repeat the level you’re stuck on, over and over and repeatedly failing soon gets frustrating. Once you’ve used any boosters you’ve accrued, (and they aren’t generous, at all, with those), the only option in order to continue the game is to spend money on extra time or boosters. There’s no way to earn more, either by watching ads, or playing side quests, or replaying earlier levels. Having just spent around £10 trying to get past two extremely difficult levels, I’m probably going to delete the game now. I don’t like games that force me to spend money to progress. I’ll spend on extras and additional beneficial content, but I don’t like being forced to spend just to be able to continue with the game. It’s a shame.

title: Good game but challenging
content:
I try hard to fund my game purchases through advert consumption rather than cash.  And so far so good on this game.   I am a patient individual so I will try the same level several times rather than use the boosters.  I also play this competitively against my wife (same level - ready steady go).  Level 88 proved almost insurmountable but after being stuck at that for 2 days (probably 20 or so attempts) finally managed to clear it without using boosters of any kind.  Very satisfying.  Never found the bombshell too problematic - just have to concentrate on clearing them down before the rest.  I like that the timer does not start till you move a piece so you can look at a level for a bit before tackling it. Very good game.  Hope the levels continue to become more challenging.   I would like the option to go to an earlier level to show others, but only a minor observation.

(Extra comment added months later).  Well this game is still holding my attention - now up to level 294 without using any boosters.  

The adds, of course, are annoying to some extent.  However it pays for the game - so you choose between adds or paying.  That’s fair.  Plus you don’t actually need to watch the adds - just kick them off and use the time to stretch your fingers (needed) and focus for the next attempt.  You can also rack up spare lives by kicking off adds repeatedly (up to 5) whilst actually watching a good Netflix (other channels are available) series :).  That will help give a good run at a tricky level.  

Oh yes - for those who complain about the nature of the advert shown - do realise that it’s not the game which selects the advert - it’s driven by your historic use of the computer / phone on that account.

title: A good and challenging game…
content:
First of all the good bits:
It’s not necessary to spend to progress, admittedly some levels are tricky and can take a long time to crack, but that’s a good thing, it wouldn’t be rewarding if there was no challenge.

Currently I am on level 196 and I haven’t spent anything.  (Update, 2 days spent to finally beat level 196, now passing level 206 still not spent a penny)

Now the bad bits, to be honest there isn’t much, but it takes 30 minutes to recover a single life, and you can only get 5, so the developers are actually limiting how long you can actually play the game. I don’t have a huge issue with that per se, but on challenging levels it becomes frustrating because it’s very easy to forget a sequence so lives get wasted trying to get beyond a certain spot.  So perhaps offering a shorter life building time, say 15 minutes would be better, the occasions that you get infinite lives can help, but in reality these tend to fall at a point of easier levels so don’t really help. Alternatively allow players to use the infinite life periods at their discretion.

Also, developers lower your prices and you might find your income increases, I wouldn’t mind paying £3-4 for the monthly golden ticket, but not £10, that’s just bonkers.

title: Fun but needs improvement
content:
This game is fun but it gets very frustrating at times. It would be great if the following changes could be made:
- You only get 5 lives, and new lives are granted only every half hour. That’s way too long, so the time between new lives should be shortened to every 10 minutes or so.
- Unlike other people, I enjoy the timer. But some of the more difficult games have way too little time to complete the round. As the levels increase, so should the time.
- Because there is a timer, there should be a warning given when you’re down to 20 seconds, and then again at 10 seconds. That way you can choose to use the extra time booster before time is up (if you have one).
- As time is running out, it is harder to move the pieces. It doesn’t matter how hard I press, it just won’t grab, and it makes it that much longer to complete the round. That needs to be fixed as it is very very frustrating.
- You cannot sync your progress between 2 devices. I would pay for no ads, except that I play equally on both my phone and my tablet. I’m not paying twice. This has to be changed.
- I got free boosters when I first started, but there isn’t much opportunity to earn more. 

As I said, I have been enjoying the game, but as I move up in levels, it’s getting far too frustrating. If the above changes are made, I would rate the game 5 stars. If changes aren’t made, I will delete the game.

title: Almost Perfect
content: I really REALLY like this game. Not swamped with ads; no push to purchase; great graphics and good challenges adn game innovations. THE ONLY thing I would change would be to add the ability to turn off the clock. I am recuperating from illness, and I find working against the clock to be stressful. Personally, I would enjoy the game SO MUCH MORE if, quite simply, the challenge of clearing the board WAS the challenge. I understand some people need the stress stimulation of limited time/limited moves scenario - and keep that option for those people; but PLEASE: soften the game for those of us who don’t want a stress attack!! It has value in its most simplistic form - the game is THAT good. Well Done. P.S: I realise your income likely comes from ads when we fail a level. As such, I would be prepared to pay for a version that could toggle the timer off or on as desired - And STILL watch adds when I have completed a level.
